skill.description: Azure Identity SDK guidance for .NET applications using Microsoft Entra ID. Covers DefaultAzureCredential, managed identity, service principals, developer credentials, and common authentication patterns.

security_audit.summary: The skill is a single Markdown reference file for Azure.Identity usage and does not include executable scripts or hidden automation. Static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline SDK names, placeholder Azure credential variables, example service URLs, and reference links. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

content.value_statement: Azure authentication in .NET has many credential choices and production tradeoffs. This skill gives concise patterns for Azure.Identity, DefaultAzureCredential, managed identity, and service principals.
actual_capabilities: Lists package installation commands for Azure.Identity, Microsoft.Extensions.Azure, and Azure.Identity.Broker.
Shows DefaultAzureCredential usage with Azure Storage and ASP.NET Core dependency injection.
Explains managed identity, service principal, certificate, and developer credential options.
Provides examples for sovereign cloud authority hosts and custom credential chains.
Summarizes error handling, retry configuration, thread safety, and supported Azure services.
Links to official Microsoft documentation, API references, NuGet, and source code.
limitations: It is reference guidance, not a complete application template.
It does not verify the installed Azure.Identity package version in a project.
It cannot validate tenant settings, role assignments, or managed identity configuration.
Version notes may become stale and should be checked against official Microsoft sources.

use_cases.title: Add Azure SDK authentication
use_cases.description: Use the skill to add DefaultAzureCredential to a .NET service that calls Azure Storage or Key Vault.

use_cases.title: Plan production identity strategy
use_cases.description: Compare managed identity, service principals, certificates, and credential chains before deploying to Azure.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot authentication failures
use_cases.description: Review exception types, logging options, and credential availability when Azure authentication fails.

prompt_templates.title: Start with DefaultAzureCredential
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to use Azure.Identity DefaultAzureCredential in a .NET app that connects to Azure Blob Storage.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a credential type
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare managed identity, ClientSecretCredential, ClientCertificateCredential, and AzureCliCredential for my .NET service.

prompt_templates.title: Configure dependency injection
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me register Azure Storage and Key Vault clients in ASP.NET Core using Microsoft.Extensions.Azure and DefaultAzureCredential.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production credential chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure Azure.Identity credential approach for production and local development, including logging, retries, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to authenticate a .NET app to Azure Blob Storage.
output_examples.output: The response recommends Azure.Identity, DefaultAzureCredential, package installation, and a Blob service client setup.

output_examples.input: A cloud team needs production guidance for Azure-hosted workloads.
output_examples.output: The response explains why managed identity is preferred and when user-assigned identity is appropriate.

output_examples.input: A service reports authentication failures during startup.
output_examples.output: The response suggests checking credential availability, tenant configuration, exception types, and Azure Identity diagnostic logging.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity for Azure-hosted production workloads.
Use deterministic credential choices in production instead of broad local developer chains.
Reuse credential instances across Azure SDK clients and enable diagnostics during troubleshooting.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode client secrets, tenant identifiers, or certificate passwords in source code.
Do not enable interactive browser authentication in unattended production services.
Do not assume DefaultAzureCredential uses the same source in every environment.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.Identity authentication patterns for .NET applications using Microsoft Entra ID.

faq.question: Does it create credentials or Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must configure Azure resources and permissions separately.

faq.question: Is DefaultAzureCredential always recommended?
faq.answer: It is useful for many scenarios, but production services often need a specific credential type.

faq.question: Can it help with managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows system-assigned and user-assigned managed identity patterns for Azure-hosted workloads.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends managed identity, credential reuse, deterministic production credentials, and careful secret handling.
